STEP 2 - Vessel: A square white plate, roughly 24 cm across in its usable area. Treating it as a 26 cm dinner plate gives an area of about 530 cm².

STEP 3 - Items: One slice of white bread. No visible spread or oil.

STEP 4 - Area: The slice is about 11 × 12 cm, roughly 130 cm², so it covers about 25% of the plate.

STEP 5 - Volume: 130 cm² × 1.3 cm thickness = 169 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams: A single slice is not a whole loaf, but it is still airy bread. I used a density of about 0.35 g/ml, which gives roughly 60 g. That fits a typical large sourdough slice. Using the bread-like slice density of 0.9 would give about 150 g, which is implausible for one slice, so I kept 0.35.

STEP 7 - Energy: White or sourdough bread is about 265 kcal per 100 g, so 60 g × 2.65 ≈ 159 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: A single large slice at about 60 g and 160 kcal is plausible.
